name: QAR overall score
purpose: Measures how far QAR as a whole is from its ideals by combining the sub-metrics QME1 to QME7, each normalised to the range zero to one by a stated rule (pass rate; pass rate scaled by cost per passing turn; the share of solutions whose selection follows a current row) and weighted by the ideals of do-grounded-work: a weight per ideal with its reason in esoi.toml [balance.metric-qar-overall], split equally over the sub-metrics that serve it. Each sub-metric has a cheap tier (offline arms, or a small sampled run of a paid arm) for the everyday QUICK score and a full tier (the whole input set, against a live model where the arm is paid, run only by decision with a budget) for the FULL score. It is computed from recorded rows only and never re-runs an arm; an arm whose row is stale, missing or not built is unmeasured and never counted as a pass.
record: Per tier: the headline (the weighted value over the measured weight only), the floor (unmeasured counted as zero), the ceiling (unmeasured counted as one) and the measured share of the weight; per sub-metric its value, tier, and the date, commit and cost of each arm's last row; and what is not measured, with the command and estimated cost that would measure it, all printed by the command. The results row counts the sub-metrics measured on current rows and at or above the bar in esoi.toml. Re-run it after any results change: it costs nothing.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the recorded_rows offline arm of qar_overall runs the whole case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read]

name: Task lifecycle correctness over offline cases
purpose: offline cases: poll, claim, run and report lifecycle (done, failed, needs-you with a decision, duplicate scan, lost claim, scheduled-not-yet-due, team scoping, unconfigured), persona selection by exact structured field, quest-folder pull and push (idempotent, human text kept, bullets pushed once), folder ownership, local-time scheduling, env-file and flag handling; fake Quest client and scripted model only, zero model calls The edge is a fake Quest client and a scripted model, so wire-level behaviour (HTTP errors, real Quest payload shapes) is not scored; the quest_client tests and the dev-Quest qualitative run pin it.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the qar_runner offline arm of run_queued_tasks runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Step continuity at cost over multi-step requests
purpose: Measures whether every step of a multi-step request acts consistently with what the request established earlier (a refusal, a correction, the resolved request, an earlier finding), at a cost the fast tier can carry. Read in this direction: maximise requests whose every step is consistent; hold the chat judge pass rate; minimise input tokens per request, counting cached tokens apart. Its cases include requests a coding agent completes, so the share the chat completes beside it is read too.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled multi-step requests: the share of requests with no inconsistent step, the chat judge pass rate, and uncached and cached input tokens per request; and the share of the coding agent's completed requests the implementation also completes; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Scripted requests are shorter than real sessions, so a failure that needs a long one may not show; cache behaviour differs by vendor and may not show offline; it cannot tell whether an item should have been admitted, which the admission metric judges.

name: Account-state consistency across scripted sessions
purpose: Measures whether what the AI says about the person's account is true when said and consistent across a session. Read in this direction: maximise state claims that match the store at reply time; allow no contradiction and no repeated or re-proposed change; minimise reads per turn. Its cases include questions about how to use the app, answered from the product documentation, and claims about what the AI can do in the app.
record: Per implementation on the same scripted sessions: the share of state claims matching the store at reply time, contradictions per session, repeated or re-proposed changes, and reads per turn; and the share of app-usage questions answered correctly and in-app capability claims that are true; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. It needs a disposable host account and the host's real operations, so it cannot run wholly offline; it sees only changes the script makes, not concurrent ones; a claim extractor decides what counts as a state claim.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the card_and_reads offline arm of act_as_the_body runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Representative long-view carry-through across assigned quests, with nothing outside its branch
purpose: Measures whether each request a representative handles starts from what its assigned quests and their intents have already settled, and whether that stays inside the representative's branch. Read in this direction: maximise multi-session cases passed (a decline on one assigned quest holds on another, a correction applies, chat and background work agree, no question asked again once declined); allow no item to reach another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person; add no time before the reply.
record: Per implementation on the same multi-session cases: the share passed, items reaching another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person, time added before the reply, and model calls per request; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet, and the hierarchy-aware fence it counts against does not exist in the library. Scripted sessions are far shorter than months of use; a pass can come from the current message rather than the long view; a wrong line in a maintained view that no case asks about is invisible; hierarchies in the cases are the author's, and a real person's may be deeper. The host's existing live checks (a declined proposal not re-proposed, retrieval scoped to the active quest) can seed the cases.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the separate_stores offline arm of hold_the_long_view runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Requests held to their ESOI metric by code
purpose: Measures whether the rule that every request applies its relevant ESOI metric holds in the flow, by code. Read in this direction: maximise the share of requests with an applicable metric that were measured before and after by code and did not regress, or whose regression was answered; maximise the share of metric-less requests for which a metric was proposed; allow no regression left without a response; add no time before a chat reply. Every count comes from the runner's ledger and records, never from a model's text.
record: Per implementation on the same replayed requests across chat turns, queued tasks and deep runs: the share measured and not regressed, the share of metric-less requests with a proposed metric, regressions left unanswered, time added before the reply, and model calls per request; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. The same shares can be read from a live lane's ledger.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. It sees that a metric was applied, not that it was the right metric or the right slice, so a weak metric applied everywhere scores well; a proposed metric may be poor and is counted the same as a good one; a recorded row the worker wrote counts less than a measured one only if the arm says so; whether the person's own quest metric later moved takes weeks and is outside it.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the deep_runs_only offline arm of think_critically runs the whole case set with no model call]

name: Parity of Quest operations across access points
purpose: Ensures that an operation on Quest's data gives the same result whether it is reached in the same process as Quest or over its HTTP API.
record: Would record, for each operation, the result and typed outcome returned through each access point on the same account state, so the two can be compared; no command or component exists yet to produce it, so nothing is recorded today.

name: Ways in that pass their own metric
purpose: Every way a request reaches the runner is measured and passing.
record: The share of the solutions beneath take-in-the-world whose latest whole-stage row passes their own metric's gate.
disadvantages: Says nothing about a request that falls between two channels; that is answer-end-to-end's metric.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the latest whole-stage row of the metric of every solution beneath take-in-the-world passes its gate, read from esoi/results.csv with no run]

name: Context handed to the planner
purpose: Measures whether the context the area hands over is the context its members chose. Read in this direction: maximise lines that return exactly what the owning member returned; add no model call and no time before the reply.
record: Per implementation on scripted seats: the share of lines whose result equals the member's own result; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Proves delegation on scripted members, not that the chosen context is the right one, which the members' own metrics measure; two cases only.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the per_lane_assembly offline arm of context_choice runs the whole case set with no model call] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read]
